## Before you start

- **Designed for:** learners with little or no programming experience.
- **You are ready when:** you can use a web browser and are willing to predict,
  run, explain, and change small examples. No mathematics prerequisite is
  assumed.
- **Practice setup:** start with generated Colab notebooks. The required Local
  Python Tools lesson explains local workflows before units that use project
  environments and command-line tools.

::: {.callout-note title="Required does not mean install everything immediately"}
Local Python Tools is required because every learner should understand the
workflow and be able to choose a practice environment. You can complete its
browser-based comparisons before installing local software, then return to the
setup steps when Unit 4 begins.
:::

## What you will be able to do

- trace values through decisions, loops, collections, and functions;
- choose data structures and function boundaries that make behavior explainable;
- read tracebacks, reduce failures, validate input, and work safely with files;
- organize a repeatable project with dependencies, a CLI, tests, typing, and CI;
- use classes, generators, decorators, context managers, logging, and
  configuration when they improve the design;
- build and defend a small complete Python project using evidence from tests,
  output, explanations, and debugging records.

## Required learning sequence

Python Foundations curriculum version 2 has five instructional units and one
final-project unit. Complete them in order: later checkpoints deliberately reuse
earlier skills.

::: {.course-grid}
::: {.course-card}
### 1. [Programming Essentials](units/programming-essentials/index.qmd)

Run Python deliberately; use values, text, decisions, indentation, loops, and tracing.
:::

::: {.course-card}
### 2. [Data and Reusable Logic](units/data-and-reusable-logic/index.qmd)

Choose useful collections and create focused, testable functions around structured data.
:::

::: {.course-card}
### 3. [Debugging, Files, and Validation](units/debugging-files-validation/index.qmd)

Investigate failures, work safely with external files, and validate incoming data.
:::

::: {.course-card}
### 4. [Building Reliable Python Projects](units/reliable-python-projects/index.qmd)

Organize environments, modules, CLIs, tests, quality tools, and automation.
:::

::: {.course-card}
### 5. [Abstraction and Reusable Patterns](units/abstraction-and-reusable-patterns/index.qmd)

Use OOP and reusable patterns when they make a program clearer and safer.
:::

::: {.course-card}
### 6. [Python Foundations Project](project/index.qmd)

Integrate the complete course in one small, explainable, tested project.
:::
:::

## Completion requirements and assessment

Python Foundations curriculum version 2 is locally complete when you have:

1. completed all **38 required lessons**;
2. recorded all **five required unit checkpoints** after meeting their knowledge
   and practical thresholds;
3. built the required [Python Foundations Project](project/index.qmd) and
   self-assessed every rubric row as **Meets the requirement**.

Lesson quizzes remain formative and do not have a stored grade. There are no
optional lessons in this course: the sequence is the published Foundations
pathway, while extra exploration inside a lesson remains your choice.

::: {.callout-important title="Local completion is not a verified certificate"}
The completion dashboard is a private, self-reported browser record. It does not
verify identity, submit checkpoint artifacts, grade the project, or issue a
certificate. A verifiable certificate remains planned as a separate service.
:::

## Practice and next step

Treat each lesson as a lab: predict, run, explain, modify, and keep evidence.
Each unit checkpoint combines several lessons, and the final project connects
all five instructional units.
